note: R3 (#2733 increment 3, research 0021 row 11): raising an ordered resource allowance does not change the meaning of an already completed judgment. This table declares, for every LimitKind, the fields that carry it, or why R3 does not raise it. Each core's exhaustive match over LimitKind is compared against it (rs: logos_kernel::seam::allowances; go and ts: #2733 increment 3c), and the conformance harness reads the check carriers to raise a case's limits on every core's CLI (seat:caa's ruling on #2733 3b, C1 condition 2). Field names are the snake_case names the rs structs and a vector case's `limits` use. `run` fields live on RunLimits, `check` fields on CheckLimits (their names are CheckLimits::budgets()), and `bounds` fields on a bottom-up engine's own ceilings. `cores` says which carrier groups each core has, and for an absent group the reason (seat:caa's ruling on #2733 3c, condition 1): a core compares its match against the rows restricted to its groups, and its match names the reason for a kind carried only by an absent group. `raised` is the value R3 raises a field to: u32::MAX, the largest allowance every target carries, since the wasm32 guest reads a checker budget as a 32-bit usize.

reasons.not_deterministic: a wall-clock budget is not deterministic: whether a run stops on the clock depends on the machine and its load, so two runs under one budget need not agree, and R3 compares runs
reasons.no_native_engine: the core runs no native bottom-up engine: its bottom-up work is the wasm guest's, whose own ceilings no request sets, so no field on this core carries them
